ai.title: AI Question Paper Generator for Pakistani Teachers | Exam Builder
ai.description: Use AI-assisted question preparation from teaching text and instructions. Review questions, select the right chapters and create a printable school paper.
ai.heading: AI-assisted question preparation, with the teacher in control
ai.intro: Use Exam Builder’s available AI workflows to prepare draft questions from teaching material or generation instructions. The goal is a useful starting point for a teacher-reviewed paper, not an unverified exam produced without oversight.

sections.heading: Choose the source and curriculum
sections.text: Start from the class, subject and chapters your assessment covers. Use the available paste-text, generation or past-paper extraction workflow. Input options depend on the workflow and permissions; check what is available in your account.

sections.heading: Review the draft questions
sections.text: Check each proposed question for accuracy, syllabus relevance, language and difficulty. Review answer options carefully: a plausible-looking option or explanation can still be wrong. Edit or remove unsuitable material before importing it into the paper.

sections.heading: Reuse the question bank carefully
sections.text: The review tools can identify or attach existing bank questions instead of inserting another copy. Reusing an existing question preserves its recorded contributor; new manual contributions retain the actual submitting teacher.

sections.heading: Finish with a print review
sections.text: After selecting questions, check marks, ordering, diagrams, Urdu/English content and the paper layout. Keep the current textbook and teaching objectives as the authority for the final exam.

questions.q: Does AI guarantee correct or official board questions?
questions.a: No. AI can produce errors and does not predict official examinations. Teachers must review generated questions and confirm any board-pattern or syllabus requirements independently.

languages.title: Urdu & English Question Paper Maker in Pakistan | Exam Builder
languages.description: Prepare Urdu, English and dual-medium question papers using available language content, editable layouts and a print preview for your school.
languages.heading: Prepare Urdu and English question papers with care
languages.intro: Pakistani classrooms work in different mediums. Exam Builder supports paper-preparation workflows with Urdu and English question content and layout choices, so teachers can review a paper in the language their students study.

sections.heading: Select suitable question content
sections.text: Choose questions that already have the required language text where available. Do not assume every bank question has a complete Urdu and English version. Check terminology against the book used in your class.

sections.heading: Review a dual-medium paper
sections.text: When using a dual-medium layout, compare both versions of each question. The meaning, quantities, options and marks should agree. A translation should not accidentally reveal an answer or change the difficulty.

sections.heading: Check right-to-left text before printing
sections.text: Look at Urdu punctuation, mixed English terms, equation direction, numbering and line breaks in the print preview. Fonts and printer settings can affect how a final page appears.

sections.heading: Keep school branding readable
sections.text: Add your school name and optional logo through the school profile. Review the header, class details, time and total marks along with the question text. A clean layout helps students understand the paper.

questions.q: Does this mean the entire application is available in Urdu?
questions.a: These public information pages are available in English and Urdu. Paper-language capabilities depend on the available question text and layout settings; this does not promise that every account screen or question is translated.

questions.q: Can I make an Urdu paper from any English question automatically?
questions.a: Do not assume an automatic translation is complete or correct. Use available Urdu content or review and edit a translation before including it in an assessment.

guide.title: How to Create a Question Paper Online for Your School | Exam Builder
guide.description: Follow a practical school-paper workflow: select class, subject and chapters, review questions, set marks and layout, then save and print.
guide.heading: How to create a question paper online
guide.intro: A good school test starts with what students were taught. This guide follows Exam Builder’s school-paper workflow and highlights the checks a teacher should make before an assessment reaches the classroom.

sections.heading: 1. Set up your school account
sections.text: Register as the school owner, select your board and add the school name. A logo is optional. Verify the owner’s email, then add teacher accounts and permissions if other staff will prepare papers.

sections.heading: 2. Choose class, subject and chapters
sections.text: Open Generate Paper from the dashboard. Select the relevant class, subject or book and chapters from the available curriculum. Confirm that these match the textbook and edition your students use.

sections.heading: 3. Select and review questions
sections.text: Use available question-bank content, add your own questions or prepare a draft through the permitted AI workflow. Review every question and answer. Balance recall, understanding and application according to your lesson objectives.

sections.heading: 4. Check marks and exam details
sections.text: Confirm the question mix, total marks, time, class and subject. Check the instructions and any choice between questions. A paper with the right questions can still be confusing if instructions or mark totals are wrong.

sections.heading: 5. Preview the complete paper
sections.text: Inspect headings, numbering, diagrams, Urdu/English text, spacing and page breaks. Check that no question or answer option is cut off. Use your browser’s print preview to review the final page arrangement.

sections.heading: 6. Save, print and review the outcome
sections.text: Save the paper to return to it later. After using the test, note questions students misunderstood because of wording or layout and improve them for future assessments. Keep real school papers within authorized account access.

questions.q: Should I select all chapters for a weekly test?
questions.a: Only include material relevant to that assessment. A weekly test and a term exam need different coverage, so begin with your teaching plan rather than choosing every available chapter.

questions.q: Can I publish my school’s saved paper as a public sample?
questions.a: Saved papers are private application content. For public examples, create a separate, deliberately reviewed sample without real student information or confidential exam material.
